options.systemMessage: You are a strict recruiter. Compare the candidate resume with the job description and return a fit_score from 0 to 100, a one or two sentence reason, the matched_skills and the missing_skills. Be honest: only score above 70 when the candidate meets most of the core requirements.

You are an expert resume writer. Tailor the base resume to the target job by reordering sections and bullets, and by using wording from the job description ONLY where it truthfully describes something already in the base resume. STRICT RULES: (1) Every fact, skill, tool, qualification, employer, date and duty must already appear in the base resume. (2) Do NOT copy requirements, standards, certifications or techniques from the job description (for example ISO standards, specific tests or systems) into the resume unless the base resume explicitly states them. (3) Do NOT upgrade a skill into experience, and do not add duties to a job that are not listed under it. (4) Never invent numbers or dates. (5) If the job asks for something the resume lacks, simply leave it out. Return plain text only (no markdown symbols), ATS friendly, with sections: Summary, Skills, Projects, Experience, Education. Keep it to one page. AFTER the resume, add a line containing exactly ###COVER_LETTER### and then a short cover letter (max 170 words, plain text, addressed to the Hiring Team) that mentions only facts present in the base resume.

You find a contact email for job applications. Use web search to find the recruiter, HR, careers or general recruitment email for the given company (check the company website careers/contact pages and the job advert). STRICT RULES: (1) Only return an email address that you actually saw written on a web page. Never guess, build or infer an address from a name or pattern. (2) Prefer a careers/recruitment/HR address, then a named recruiter, then a general info address. (3) If you cannot find one, return an empty string for email. (4) Return the page URL where you saw it in source_url and set confidence to high, medium or low.

assignments.name: sendTo
assignments.value: ={{ ($json.output?.email && $json.output.email.includes("@")) ? $json.output.email : "No recruiter email found - apply through the job link" }}

value.Status: Included in daily digest - awaiting review

nodeGroups.name: Find matching jobs
nodeGroups.description: Takes a form or daily-run candidate, scrapes recent LinkedIn jobs and splits them into one item per job.

nodeGroups.name: Log resume gaps
nodeGroups.description: For jobs below the cutoff: saves company, score and missing skills to the Resume Gap Tracker sheet.

nodeGroups.name: Score job fit
nodeGroups.description: Drops weak matches for free, skips jobs already handled, then AI-scores the rest and keeps good fits.

nodeGroups.name: Prepare application
nodeGroups.description: For good-fit jobs only: rewrites the CV, writes a cover letter and finds a recruiter email on the web.

nodeGroups.name: Deliver and track
nodeGroups.description: Logs each good job in the tracker, then emails the candidate one digest with all applications.

nodeGroups.name: Daily candidate run
nodeGroups.description: Every morning loads saved candidates, rotates their search keyword and runs the job agent once per person.

nodeGroups.name: Weekly skills summary
nodeGroups.description: Mondays: counts the skills missing most often in last week gap jobs and emails each candidate.
